findings.title: Per-force timing breakdown is deferred, but the slice plan assigns it to this slice
findings.description: The slice plan entry for (141) (`140-slices.simulation-scaling.md:26`) says the harness reports timings "broken down by phase (spatial build, spatial query, CSR assembly, **force totals per force**, integration)". The slice records `force_total` as a single number and says "Slice 142 introduces per-force timings." Slice 142 is a Quadrants evaluation slice, and the plan does not give it harness work. Deferring this pushes harness schema changes into 142 and breaks the "JSON report schema stable from this slice" promise at line 530. The risk section (lines 697-703) also admits that `force_total` mixes profile-attribute setup with force work at small N. Recommendation: put per-force timing into this slice now, as `force_breakdown: dict[str, int]` keyed by force name and populated by the NumPy runner. The instrumented tick already loops over the force list, so the extra cost is small. Alternatively, record the deferral as an explicit, agreed change to the slice plan.

findings.title: "One file, zero changes elsewhere" conflicts with what slice 142 needs
findings.description:
The Integration Requirements say slice 142 can register a `quadrants` backend "by adding one file … and zero changes elsewhere in the harness." Two parts of the design contradict this:
1. Lines 292-296 say slice 142 will extend `PhaseTimings` with per-force data. That means editing `runner.py`, `json_report.py` and `markdown_report.py`, and bumping `schema_version` (line 531).
2. In the slice plan, slice 142 benchmarks *one force* (cohesion) as a Quadrants kernel against its NumPy and Numba versions. The `BackendRunner` abstraction works at the level of a whole tick (`tick_once() -> (TickResult, PhaseTimings)`). A tick where only one force runs on a different backend, or a benchmark of a single force kernel, does not fit that interface. The design doesn't say how 142's measurement would go through the registry.

Fix this by solving per-force timing here (see the previous finding) and by stating how a run that mixes force backends, or measures one force, plugs into `BackendRunner`. If that can't be done, drop the "zero changes" claim.

findings.title: The Numba backend is attributed to the wrong slice
findings.description: Line 341 says "Slice 144 registers `numba`…", and the Integration Requirement at lines 589-591 repeats this. Line 92 says "slice 144 / 118 territory". In the slice plan, (144) is *Quadrants Force Kernels*. Numba comes from (118) Numba Force JIT in plan 100. Slice (142) depends on (118) and needs a Numba baseline to make its go/no-go comparison. The frontmatter `interfaces` lists 142–145 but leaves out 118, so the slice that must deliver the Numba runner never sees this contract. Fix the attribution (118, or 142 as the first consumer) and add 118 to `interfaces`.

findings.title: A SHA-256 parity hash cannot do the tolerance-based parity check slice 145 needs
findings.description: Line 533 says "Slice 145's tick-level parity test consumes the harness's NumPy parity hash as the reference." The slice plan defines slice 145's parity as "full-tick parity against the NumPy reference … **within a documented tolerance** for non-deterministic GPU reductions." Lines 471-473 say that for GPU backends "a downstream consumer interprets [the hash] within the documented tolerance band." A cryptographic hash has no tolerance: any difference in the last bit gives an unrelated digest. So the hash can only detect exact matches, which tells you nothing for GPU backends. Either remove the claim that slice 145 consumes the hash, or have the harness optionally save the final `positions` and `velocities` arrays (e.g. `.npy` next to the JSON) so a later consumer can do a tolerance comparison. Also make the timing consistent: line 81 says the hash is taken "post-warmup" and line 460 says "after the measure phase".

findings.title: Phase instrumentation copies the whole tick algorithm, and the doc contradicts itself about calling `tick()`
findings.description: `tick_instrumented()` is described as "Same algorithm … with `time.perf_counter_ns()` brackets". In practice that is a copy of the full `tick()` body living in `bench/`, not "~5 lines per phase". That goes against the project's "Do not duplicate logic" rule. The risk section (lines 682-695) also concedes that drift in phase boundaries "is not detectable mechanically." The document also contradicts itself: lines 131-132 and 541 say "The harness's NumPy runner calls `tick()` directly", while lines 496-501 put a separate `tick_instrumented` in `numpy_backend.py`. Option A was rejected because of "if timer: branches", but a hook that defaults to a no-op adds no branches to the production path and keeps one copy of the algorithm. If B is kept, state plainly that the tick body is copied, fix lines 131-132 and 541, and keep the bit-equality test from line 688 as a required success criterion. Right now it appears only as a risk mitigation.

findings.title: Failure handling is missing for several I/O paths
findings.description:
The failure-mode list covers workload loading, registry lookup and `setup` exceptions. It does not cover these paths, which the design itself introduces:
- **`git rev-parse HEAD` fails.** This happens with no git, a detached or archive checkout, or a dirty tree. `git_sha` is a required header field (line 233). The doc doesn't say whether the run fails or writes a placeholder that is obviously wrong. The no-silent-fallback rule requires one or the other to be stated. A dirty working tree also makes `git_sha` misleading.
- **`tick_once` raises mid-measure.** The doc doesn't say whether a partial report is written or the run aborts. The try/finally covers only `setup` (line 514).
- **Writing to `bench/results/` fails.** The directory may be missing (it is gitignored, so it won't exist on a fresh clone), or it may lack write permission.
- **Malformed or unknown-version JSON files in `bench/results/`.** The Markdown renderer reads every backend's results from that directory (line 440). A corrupt file, or a file whose `schema_version` it doesn't recognise, needs defined behavior. Line 532 says only that readers "must reject".

State how each of these is handled and how it shows up to the user (stderr or exit code). Add tests for the git-SHA path and the bad-result-file path.

findings.title: Which results the cross-backend Markdown table combines is undefined
findings.description: The Markdown report is "one table per workload across all backends in `bench/results/`". That directory piles up runs from different timestamps, git SHAs and platforms. The doc doesn't say which file is chosen per backend (latest? same `git_sha`? same platform?). Putting rows from different commits or machines in one table produces comparisons that look valid but aren't, which undermines the slice's stated purpose ("on which platform"). Specify the selection rule. For example: the latest run per backend that matches the current `git_sha` and platform. Or limit the table to backends run in the current invocation (`--all-backends`).

findings.title: PropulsionForce is missing from the force set
findings.description: The slice lists "the five existing `BulkForce` implementations" and leaves out PropulsionForce. The slice plan's entry for (144) lists PropulsionForce among the existing forces. The architecture's baseline profile says "4 forces". If the live default config uses propulsion, `mid-flock` is not "roughly equivalent to the live-server default" (line 354). Check the force inventory and align the workloads with it.

findings.title: Platform metadata is too coarse for comparing results across machines
findings.description: `platform.processor()` returns just "arm" on macOS, and nothing records the GPU or device. Tier 3 validation "on CUDA via (141)" and comparisons between M3 and M4 need a device identifier. Consider letting each `BackendRunner` report its own device-info dict now, so adding it later doesn't force a schema version bump.

findings.title: Small internal inconsistencies
findings.description:
- Line 76 says the JSON is "one record per `(workload, backend, phase)`". The schema at lines 408-437 is one file per run, with all phases nested inside it.
- The `TPS < 1` warning threshold (line 516) is a magic number. Define it as a named constant.
- The plan entry allows CSV or JSON, so JSON alone is fine.
